summary: Hidenori Sakuma specializes in Buddhist studies and Indology. He studied at the University of Tokyo and earned his PhD at the University of Hamburg under Lambert Schmithausen. He held positions at International Buddhist University, Taisho University, and the University of Tsukuba.

Hideo Mineshima (1927–2013) worked in Buddhist studies and philosophy. He studied at Yamagata High School, Taisho University, and Waseda University. He was a longtime professor at Waseda University (1968–1998) and taught at Bunkyo Gakuin University (~1991–2003).
Hideo Murai is a scholar in Japanology and Buddhist studies. In 2000, he was attested as a professor at Otani University and served as a committee member for the Otani Academic Society.

Hideomi Yaita (born 1953) is an Indologist and Buddhist studies scholar who completed doctoral studies at Taisho University. He served as a research assistant at the Naritasan Institute for Buddhist Studies (1991–1995) and lecturer at Taisho University (1995).
Hidetaka Fukazawa (born 1956) is a religious studies scholar. He studied at Tokyo University of Foreign Studies from circa 1974 to 1979 and held a post at Hitotsubashi University around 1993.
Hidetaka Nakatani is a scholar of Buddhist studies and Indology. He studied at Kyoto University in 1966 under the supervision of Gadjin M. Nagao.
Hideto Ono (born 1944) focuses on Buddhist studies and Sinology. He studied at Komazawa University and served as an assistant professor at Aichi Gakuin University (attested 1991).

Hidetomo Yoshizawa is a scholar of Buddhist studies. He has held several posts at Taisho University, serving as a researcher (1998), research student (2006), lecturer (2008), and chief research fellow (2017).

Hidetsugu Yagi (1886–1976) studied at Kitano High School and the University of Tokyo (~1906–1909). He held posts at the University of Tokyo, Tohoku University (~1919–1932), Osaka University (~1932–1946), and Tokyo Institute of Technology (~1942–1944), and taught Arthur Waley.

Hideyo Ogawa (born 1954) is a scholar of Indology and philosophy. He studied at Hiroshima University (~1973–1981), where he later served as an assistant professor (~1989–1998) and professor of Indian Philosophy (~1998–2019).
Hideyuki Matsumori is a scholar of Buddhist studies and Indology. He completed doctoral studies at Soka University (attested 2006) and later held an assistant post there (attested 2015).

Hildegard Diemberger (born 1962) specializes in Tibetology. She conducted research supervised by Luciano Petech and Ernst Steinkellner, and has taught Michela Clemente, Lobsang Yongdan, and Adrian Zenz.

Himanshu Prabha Ray (born 1947) works in Indology and archaeology. Educated at Panjab University, JNU, and Cambridge, she was associate professor at JNU (~1986–2012) and served as Chairperson of the National Monuments Authority (~2012–2015).

Hinrich Middeldorpf (1788–1861) was a linguistics and religious studies scholar. He studied at Gelehrtenschule des Johanneums and the University of Göttingen (~1807–1810) and held a post at the University of Breslau from circa 1815 to 1861.

Hiram W. Woodward is an art historian and Buddhist studies scholar. He studied at Harvard and Yale, taught at the University of Michigan (1972–1982) and University of Vermont (~1982–1986), and was curator of Asian Art at Walters Art Museum (1986–2003).

Hirananda Sastri (1878–1946) was an Indologist and archaeologist. Educated at DAV College, Oriental College, and Panjab University, he held posts at the Archaeological Survey of India, several museums, and Baroda State's Department of Archaeology (1934–1942).
Hiroaki Yokoyama is a Buddhist studies scholar who pursued doctoral studies (attested 2013) and served as a research student at Taisho University.

Hirofumi Isoda (born 1938) is a scholar of Buddhist studies and Indology. He completed doctoral studies at Tohoku University (~1963–1966), where he served as a lecturer (~1970–1976) and associate professor (~1976–2002).
Hirofumi Toda (1936–2003) specialized in Buddhist studies and Indology. He studied under Seiren Matsunami and served as a professor at Tokushima University from circa 1980 to 2000.
Hiroko Kawanami works in religious and Buddhist studies. She studied under John Okell and Anna J. Allott, and served as a senior lecturer at Lancaster University (attested 2013–2016).
